En-gannim was a town in the lowland (Shephelah) of Judah, listed among the cities allotted to the tribe of Judah in Josh 15:34, where it appears between Zanoah and Tappuah. Its name means "spring of gardens." Nothing else is recorded about it in the Bible. The name is shared by another place, a…

En-haddah was a town in the territory given to the tribe of Issachar when the land was divided under Joshua. It is mentioned only once, in the list of Issachar's towns, where it appears next to En-gannim, Remeth and Beth-pazzez (Josh 19:21). Smith's Bible Dictionary and the International Standard…

En-hakkore was a spring at Lehi in Judah that, according to Judg 15:19, God opened from a hollow place after Samson had killed a thousand Philistines with a donkey's jawbone. Exhausted and thirsty, Samson drank and revived, and he named the spring En-hakkore. The narrator notes that it was still…

En-hazor was a city in the territory allotted to the tribe of Naphtali, listed with Kedesh and Edrei in Josh 19:37. Smith's Bible Dictionary counts it among Naphtali's fortified cities, based on the surrounding list, and treats it as a different place from the better-known Hazor. The name means…

En-mishpat was an older name for Kadesh, a spring site in the wilderness south of Canaan. It appears only in Gen 14:7, where the four eastern kings led by Chedorlaomer turned back to En-mishpat during their campaign and then struck the country of the Amalekites and the Amorites living in…

En-rimmon was one of the towns in southern Judah where people of Judah settled after returning from exile in Babylon, listed alongside Zareah and Jarmuth (Neh 11:29). The name probably means “spring of the pomegranate.” Smith's Bible Dictionary and the International Standard Bible Encyclopedia both…

En-tappuah, meaning "spring of the apple" (or "apple spring"), was a spring on the border of the tribe of Manasseh. Joshua 17:7 traces Manasseh's boundary from Asher to Michmethah, near Shechem, and then along to the inhabitants of En-tappuah. By inference from the following verse, it was probably…

Enam was a town in the lowland (Shephelah) of Judah. It is listed among the towns allotted to the tribe of Judah, alongside Zanoah, Engannim and Tappuah (Josh 15:34). This is its only mention in the Bible, and nothing is recorded about events there. Smith's Bible Dictionary gives the meaning of the…

Eneglaim was a place on the shore of the Dead Sea, named only once in the Bible, in Ezekiel's vision of the restored land. In that vision a river flows from the temple and turns the salt water fresh, so that fishermen spread their nets along the shore "from Engedi even unto Eneglaim" (Ezek 47:10).…

Ephah was a people and region of northern Arabia, named in Isa 60:6 alongside Midian and Sheba as sources of the camels and dromedaries that would come to Jerusalem bearing gold and incense. STEPBible Proper Names (Tyndale House) describes Ephah as an Arabian tribe known for its camels. Its pairing…

Ephes-dammim was the place in Judah where the Philistines camped before the battle in which David fought Goliath. It lay between Shochoh and Azekah, in the hill country west of Bethlehem overlooking the valley of Elah (1 Sam 17:1). Easton's Bible Dictionary and Smith's Bible Dictionary identify it…

Ephraim was a town near the wilderness where Jesus went with his disciples after he stopped moving openly among the Jews (John 11:54). The surrounding chapter shows that this withdrawal followed the raising of Lazarus and the council's decision to put Jesus to death, so it was probably a retreat to…

Ephron was a place on the boundary between the tribal territories of Benjamin and Judah, west of Jerusalem. Joshua 18:15 describes Benjamin's southern border running from the edge of Kirjath-jearim to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah. The King James wording here does not use the name: where it…

Ephron was a town in the hill country north of Jerusalem, one of the places King Abijah of Judah took from Jeroboam of Israel after defeating him, along with its surrounding villages, Bethel and Jeshanah (2 Chr 13:19). The King James Version spells it "Ephrain", and the Hebrew text has both…

Esek was a well dug by Isaac's servants in the valley of Gerar, in the southern land where Isaac had settled. The herdsmen of Gerar quarreled with Isaac's herdsmen over it, claiming the water as theirs, so Isaac named the well Esek, meaning "contention" or "quarrel" (Gen 26:20). The surrounding…

Eshan was a town in the hill country of Judah, named only once, in the list of towns allotted to the tribe of Judah (Josh 15:52). The King James Version spells it "Eshean." It appears alongside Arab and Dumah in a group of towns in the uplands around Hebron. Its exact site is uncertain. Easton's…

Eshtemoh was a town in the hill country of Judah. It is named once, in the list of towns given to the tribe of Judah, between Anab and Anim (Josh 15:50). The International Standard Bible Encyclopedia treats it as the same place as Eshtemoa, a spelling found elsewhere. Under that name, connected…

Etam was a town of the tribe of Simeon, named in 1 Chr 4:32 alongside Ain, Rimmon, Tochen and Ashan as one of the villages where the Simeonites lived. It appears only in this list. The parallel list of Simeon's towns in Josh 19:7 names Ain, Remmon, Ether and Ashan, so Smith's Bible Dictionary links…

Etam was a city of Judah that King Rehoboam built up as a fortified town, listed with Bethlehem and Tekoa in 2 Chr 11:6. The surrounding passage presents it as one of the defensive cities he strengthened after the kingdom divided. Its place in that list suggests it lay near Bethlehem, in the hill…

Eth-kazin was a town on the eastern border of the tribe of Zebulun. Josh 19:13 names it in the description of that boundary, between Gath-hepher (Gittah-hepher) and Rimmon, near Neah. The King James Version spells it Ittah-kazin. The International Standard Bible Encyclopedia explains that this…

Fair Havens was a harbor on the south coast of Crete where the ship carrying Paul to Rome stopped after a difficult passage along the island, near the city of Lasea (Acts 27:8). Easton's Bible Dictionary says the ship waited there a considerable time for a favorable wind. The ship's master and…

Forest, more fully the House of the Forest, appears in Isa 22:8 as the place where Judah's armour was stored. Isaiah says that when Judah's defences were laid bare, the people looked to the weapons kept there. By inference from connected passages, this is the House of the Forest of Lebanon, a large…

Gabbatha was the place in Jerusalem where Pilate sat on the judgment seat to give his verdict at the trial of Jesus. John 19:13 calls it in Greek "the Pavement" and gives Gabbatha as its Hebrew (probably Aramaic) name, which Hitchcock's Bible Names and the International Standard Bible Encyclopedia…

Gamad is known only from Ezek 27:11, where the Gammadim (the people of Gamad) stood in the towers of Tyre and hung their shields on its walls. They appear next to the men of Arvad in Ezekiel's lament over the city. Whether Gamad was a place or a description of a group is uncertain. Easton's Bible…

Gareb was a hill near Jerusalem, mentioned only in Jer 31:39. In Jeremiah's prophecy of the city's rebuilding, a measuring line would run out over the hill Gareb and then around to Goath, marking a wider boundary for the restored city. By inference from the passage, the hill then lay outside or at…

Gate Miphkad, called the Muster Gate in the ESV, was a gate of Jerusalem in Nehemiah's time. It is mentioned only once, in the list of workers who rebuilt the city wall after the return from exile. Malchiah, a goldsmith's son, repaired the stretch of wall as far as the house of the temple servants…

n: Gate of the Children of the People
bio: The Gate of the Children of the People (called the People's Gate in some modern translations) was a gate of Jerusalem mentioned only in Jer 17:19. The LORD told Jeremiah to stand there, and then in all the gates of the city, to deliver a message about keeping the sabbath. The verse describes it as…

The Gate of the Foundation was a gate in Jerusalem, mentioned once, in the account of the priest Jehoiada's plan to crown the young Joash king in place of Queen Athaliah. Jehoiada divided the priests and Levites on duty into three groups: one at the king's house, one at the Gate of the Foundation,…

Gath-rimmon was a town in the territory of the half tribe of Manasseh west of the Jordan. Along with Taanach, it was given with its pasturelands to the Levites (Josh 21:25). The name, meaning "press of the pomegranate," is shared with a Levitical city of Dan listed just before it, and Smith's Bible…

Geba is the starting point of David's pursuit of the Philistines after his victory in the valley of Rephaim. He struck them down "from Geba until thou come to Gazer," driving them west toward the coastal plain (2 Sam 5:25). Several places in the Bible share this name. The best-known Geba is a town…

Gebim was a small town north of Jerusalem, in the territory of Benjamin, named only once in the Bible. In Isaiah's poem of an army advancing on Jerusalem (Isa 10:28–32), usually understood as the Assyrian army, its people gather to flee as the invader approaches (Isa 10:31). The name is usually…

Geder was a Canaanite city whose king appears among the thirty-one kings west of the Jordan defeated by Joshua and the Israelites. Its only mention is in that list, where it comes next to Debir (Josh 12:13). The name probably means "wall," which may suggest a walled town (Hitchcock's Bible Names;…

Gederothaim was a town in the lowland (Shephelah) of Judah, named in the list of cities given to the tribe of Judah in Josh 15:36, directly after Gederah. The name probably means "two sheepfolds" (Smith's Bible Dictionary) or "place of enclosures" (International Standard Bible Encyclopedia). The…

Gedor was a place where clans of the tribe of Simeon went looking for pasture for their flocks, reaching its entrance as far as the east side of the valley (1 Chr 4:39). The surrounding passage says they found good, quiet pasture there, drove out the earlier inhabitants, including the Meunim, and…

Geliloth was a landmark on the southern boundary of the tribe of Benjamin, where it met the territory of Judah. Josh 18:17 traces the border from En-shemesh toward Geliloth, "over against the going up of Adummim," and then down to the stone of Bohan the son of Reuben. The name means "circles" or…

Geruth Chimham was a stopping place near Bethlehem where Johanan and the Judean survivors stayed on their way to Egypt (Jer 41:17). From the surrounding chapter, this was after Ishmael murdered Gedaliah, the governor Babylon had appointed, when the group feared Babylonian reprisal. The Hebrew…

Giah was a place near Gibeon, mentioned only once in the Bible, in 2 Sam 2:24. After the battle at the pool of Gibeon, Joab and Abishai chased Abner. At sunset they reached the hill of Ammah, which lay "before Giah by the way of the wilderness of Gibeon." Giah is named only to fix where that hill…

Gibeath-elohim, meaning "hill of God," was a place in the territory of Benjamin. It is named only in 1 Sam 10:5, where Samuel tells the newly anointed Saul that he will come there. He says a Philistine garrison is stationed at the site and that Saul will meet a company of prophets coming down from…

Gibeath-haaraloth, meaning "hill of the foreskins," was the place where Joshua circumcised the Israelites with flint knives soon after they crossed the Jordan River into Canaan (Josh 5:3). The King James Version translates the name as "the hill of the foreskins" instead of giving it as a proper…

Gidom was a place named only in Judg 20:45, in the account of the war between the other Israelite tribes and Benjamin after the outrage at Gibeah. As the defeated Benjamites fled toward the wilderness and the rock of Rimmon, Israel pursued them hard as far as Gidom and killed two thousand of them…

Gilo, also spelled Giloh, was a town in the hill country of Judah. It appears here only indirectly, in the word "Gilonite" (someone from Gilo), used of Ahithophel, the father of Eliam, one of David's mighty warriors (2 Sam 23:34). Other passages give more about the town. Josh 15:51 lists Giloh…

Gimzo was a town of Judah, mentioned only once in the Bible, near the edge of the Philistine plain. It was one of several towns in the low country and the south of Judah, along with their surrounding villages, that the Philistines captured and settled. The surrounding chapter places this in the…

Goah was a place near Jerusalem, mentioned only in Jer 31:39, where the King James Version spells it Goath. In Jeremiah's prophecy of the city's future rebuilding, a measuring line goes out over the hill Gareb and then turns around to Goah, marking part of the boundary of the restored city. The…

Gog is a name that appears with Magog in Rev 20:8, where Satan, released at the end of the thousand years, goes out to deceive the nations in the four quarters of the earth, called "Gog and Magog," and gathers them for battle in numbers like the sand of the sea. The pairing draws on Ezek 38–39,…

Gudgodah was a stopping place of the Israelites during their wilderness journey. Deut 10:7 says they traveled there after leaving Mosera, where Aaron died according to the preceding verse, and went on from Gudgodah to Jotbath, described as a land of streams of water. The International Standard…

Gur was a place near Ibleam, in the hill country at the southern edge of the plain of Jezreel. It is mentioned only once, as "the going up to Gur." There Jehu's men struck King Ahaziah of Judah in his chariot as he fled after Jehu killed Joram of Israel. Ahaziah escaped to Megiddo and died there (2…

Gurbaal was a place or district where certain Arabians lived, mentioned only in 2 Chr 26:7. That verse says God helped King Uzziah of Judah against the Philistines, against these Arabians, and against the Mehunims. The name is usually taken to mean "dwelling of Baal," and Easton's Bible Dictionary…

Hadad-rimmon is a place named once, in Zech 12:11, where the prophet compares a coming great mourning in Jerusalem to "the mourning of Hadadrimmon in the valley of Megiddon." Its name combines two names of Syrian gods. Easton's and Smith's Bible Dictionaries take it as a place in the valley of…

Hadashah was a town in the territory allotted to the tribe of Judah. It appears only once, in the list of towns of the Shephelah, the lowland hills of western Judah, where it is named between Zenan and Migdalgad (Josh 15:37). The name means "new." The Mishnah, as reported by the International…

Hadrach was a region in Syria, named only once in the Bible, in Zechariah's oracle that opens "the burden of the word of the LORD in the land of Hadrach," with Damascus as its resting place (Zech 9:1). The following verses group it with Hamath, Tyre and Sidon as targets of the same judgment (Zech…

Haeleph was a town given to the tribe of Benjamin, named once in the list of Benjamin's cities in Josh 18:28. The King James Version spells it Eleph. The Hebrew form includes the definite article, "the Eleph," which gives the spelling Haeleph. It appears in the last group of fourteen cities,…

Hahiroth is a shortened form of Pi-hahiroth, the place where the Israelites camped just before passing through the sea after leaving Egypt. The International Standard Bible Encyclopedia treats it as the same place as Pi-hahiroth. In Num 33:8 the Hebrew text has the short form, though the King James…

Hakkephirim is a place named in Neh 6:2, where Sanballat and Geshem invited Nehemiah to meet them in the plain of Ono. Nehemiah understood the invitation as a plot to harm him. The Hebrew word means "the villages," and the King James Version translates it that way ("in some one of the villages").…

Halhul was a town in the hill country of Judah, listed among the towns allotted to the tribe of Judah alongside Bethzur and Gedor (Josh 15:58). The Bible mentions it only in this list. Its name survives in the modern village of Halhul, a few miles north of Hebron near the road to Jerusalem.…

Hali was a town on the border of the territory given to the tribe of Asher. It is named only once, in the list of Asher's boundary towns, between Helkath and Beten and alongside Achshaph (Josh 19:25). The Bible says nothing more about it. Its site is uncertain. The International Standard Bible…

Ham was a region east of the Jordan where Chedorlaomer and the kings allied with him defeated the Zuzim during their campaign, as described in Gen 14:5. It is named between Ashteroth Karnaim and Shaveh Kiriathaim, which suggests a place in the highlands of Transjordan along the invaders' route…

Hamath-zobah was a place in Syria that Solomon attacked and overcame, mentioned only in 2 Chr 8:3. The surrounding passage describes his building of cities, and the next verse speaks of store cities he built in Hamath. The name joins Hamath, the major city on the Orontes River, with Zobah, an…

Hammoth-dor was a city in the territory of Naphtali that was assigned, with its surrounding pasturelands, to the Levites. It was one of three such cities from Naphtali, listed with Kedesh in Galilee, a city of refuge, and Kartan (Josh 21:32). Smith's Bible Dictionary gives the name's meaning as…

Hamonah, meaning "multitude" or "horde," is the name of a city in Ezekiel's prophecy against Gog, mentioned only in Ezek 39:16. The surrounding passage describes the burial of Gog's defeated army in a valley that would be called Hamon-gog, and says the land would be cleansed in this way. Hamonah is…

Hanes was a city in Egypt, mentioned only in Isa 30:4. In a passage warning Judah against relying on Egypt for protection, Isaiah describes envoys at Zoan (Tanis) and ambassadors arriving at Hanes, probably Judah's delegation seeking an alliance with Pharaoh. Its location is uncertain. Some…

Hannathon was a town on the northern boundary of the territory given to the tribe of Zebulun. The boundary description in Josh 19:14 says the border turned around on the north side to Hannathon and ended in the valley of Jiphthahel. This is its only mention in the Bible. Smith's Bible Dictionary…

Hapharaim was a town in the territory given to the tribe of Issachar. It is named only once, in the list of Issachar's towns, alongside Shion and Anaharath (Josh 19:19). By inference from the surrounding list, which also includes Jezreel and Shunem, it lay in or near the Jezreel Valley in lower…

Hara was a region in the Assyrian empire to which Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria deported the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half tribe of Manasseh, along with Halah, Habor and the river Gozan (1 Chr 5:26). It is named only in this verse, and its location is uncertain. Easton's Bible Dictionary…

Harmon is a name that appears in Amos 4:3 in the original Hebrew and refers to the place where the wealthy women of Samaria would be thrown when their city fell. The King James Version does not treat it as a name and translates the word as "the palace." Other translations keep it as the proper name…

Hazar-addar was a town on the southern border of the land promised to Israel. In Num 34:4 it appears in the list of boundary points: the border ran south of the ascent of Akrabbim, passed on to Zin, went south to Kadesh-barnea, and continued to Hazar-addar and then Azmon. The name means "village of…

Hazar-gaddah was a town in the far south of Judah's territory, named only once, in the list of towns allotted to the tribe of Judah in Josh 15:27. It appears among the towns of the Negev near the border with Edom, between Moladah and Heshmon. Easton's Bible Dictionary places it on Judah's southern…

Hazar-susah was a town in the Negev, in the far south of Canaan, assigned to the tribe of Simeon when the land was divided (Josh 19:5). It is listed alongside Ziklag and Beth-marcaboth among the Simeonite towns that lay inside Judah's territory. Easton's Bible Dictionary gives the name's meaning as…

Hazar-susim was a town of the tribe of Simeon in the far south of Judah, the Negev region. It appears in 1 Chr 4:31 in a list of Simeonite towns, alongside Beth-marcaboth, Beth-birei and Shaaraim, which the text says were Simeon's cities until the reign of David. The name probably means "village of…

Hazer-hatticon, a name meaning "the middle village," is a place named in Ezekiel's vision of the ideal boundaries of the restored land of Israel. It appears in the description of the northern border, listed after Hamath, Berothah and Sibraim, and is said to lie "by the coast of Hauran," meaning at…

Hazor was a town in the far south of Judah, listed in Josh 15:23 among the cities of the Negev allotted to the tribe of Judah, between Kedesh and Ithnan. It is one of several places in the Bible with this name and should not be confused with the better-known Canaanite city of Hazor in the north.…

Hazor was a town in the far south of Judah, the Negev, named in the list of towns given to the tribe of Judah in Josh 15:25. The verse is hard to divide. The King James Version reads "Hazor, Hadattah, and Kerioth, and Hezron, which is Hazor," but many readers join the names differently. Smith's…

Hazor was a town in the territory of Benjamin where Benjamites lived after returning from the Babylonian exile. It appears only once, in Nehemiah's list of resettled places, alongside Ramah and Gittaim (Neh 11:33). The name was shared by several places in the Bible, including the better-known…

Hazor-hadattah, meaning "New Hazor," was a town in the far south of the territory allotted to the tribe of Judah. It appears only in Josh 15:25, among the southernmost cities of Judah "toward the coast of Edom" in the Negev. The King James Version prints "Hazor, Hadattah" as two names, but many…

Helbah was a Canaanite town in the territory given to the tribe of Asher. It appears only in Judg 1:31, in a list of towns whose inhabitants Asher did not drive out, alongside Accho, Zidon (Sidon), Ahlab, Achzib, Aphik and Rehob. The name means "fatness" or "fertile." Easton's Bible Dictionary and…

Helbon was a place known for its wine, mentioned only in Ezek 27:18. In Ezekiel's lament over Tyre, Damascus is said to have traded with Tyre in "the wine of Helbon, and white wool." The name probably means "fat" or "fertile." Older geographers linked Helbon with Aleppo (Arabic Haleb). Smith's…

Helech is a name that appears in Ezekiel’s lament over the trading city of Tyre, in a verse describing the foreign soldiers who guarded its walls (Ezek 27:11). The Hebrew word sits alongside “the men of Arvad,” and the King James Version translates it as “thine army,” so the name does not appear in…

Heleph was a town named as the starting point of the boundary of the territory given to the tribe of Naphtali (Josh 19:33). From Heleph the border ran past Allon, Zaanannim, Adami, Nekeb, Jabneel and Lakum, ending at the Jordan. The name has been taken to mean "exchange" (Easton's and Smith's Bible…

Heliopolis, Greek for "city of the sun," was an ancient Egyptian city that was a major center for worship of the sun god. In Jer 43:13, Jeremiah warns that the king of Babylon would break the sacred images of "Bethshemesh" ("house of the sun") in Egypt and burn the Egyptians' temples. This…

Helkath-hazzurim was a field at Gibeon, north of Jerusalem, where twelve of Abner's men, fighting for Saul's son Ish-bosheth, met twelve of Joab's men, fighting for David, in a contest of champions. Each man seized his opponent by the head and drove his sword into his side, so they all fell…

Heres is a place named in Judg 8:13 as the point from which Gideon son of Joash turned back after defeating the Midianite kings Zebah and Zalmunna. The King James Version reads the Hebrew phrase as "before the sun was up," since heres can mean "sun." The Revised Version and the International…

Hereth (spelled Hareth in the King James Version) was a forest or wooded area in the land of Judah where David went while fleeing from King Saul. The prophet Gad told David to leave "the hold", by inference from the surrounding passage his refuge near Mizpeh in Moab, and go into Judah, so David…

Heshmon was a town in the far south of Judah, named once in the list of cities given to the tribe of Judah in the Negev region toward the border of Edom (Josh 15:27). It appears between Hazar-gaddah and Beth-pelet, and nothing else is recorded about it. Easton's Bible Dictionary gives the name's…

Hezron was a landmark on the southern border of Judah, named in the boundary description between Kadesh-barnea and Adar (Josh 15:3). The border ran past the Ascent of Akrabbim and the wilderness of Zin, up to Kadesh-barnea, on to Hezron, then up to Adar and around to Karkaa. The name probably means…

Hierapolis, meaning "holy city" according to Hitchcock's Bible Names, was a city of Phrygia in the Lycus valley of western Asia Minor. Its only biblical mention is in Col 4:13. There Paul says that Epaphras worked hard for the believers in Colossae, Laodicea and Hierapolis, which implies that a…

Hilen was a town in the hill country of Judah, named in 1 Chr 6:58 among the cities and their surrounding pasture lands given to the descendants of Aaron the priest. In the parallel list of priestly cities in Josh 21:15, and in the list of Judah's towns in Josh 15:51, the name appears as Holon, and…

Hill Mizar, called Mount Mizar in modern translations, is a hill named only once in the Bible, in Ps 42:6. There the psalmist, feeling downcast, says he will remember God "from the land of Jordan, and of the Hermonites, from the hill Mizar." The setting suggests a spot in the far north, near the…

Hobah was a place near Damascus, the farthest point to which Abram and his servants chased the defeated forces of the eastern kings after a night attack (Gen 14:15). From the surrounding chapter, this was the campaign in which Abram rescued his nephew Lot, who had been taken captive when Sodom was…

Holon was a town of Moab on the "plain country," the high tableland east of the Dead Sea. It appears only in Jeremiah's oracle against Moab, where it is named with Jahazah and Mephaath as places on which judgment has come (Jer 48:21). The International Standard Bible Encyclopedia suggests it was…

Horem was a city in the territory allotted to the tribe of Naphtali, named in Josh 19:38 alongside Iron, Migdalel, Bethanath and Bethshemesh. It is one of the nineteen cities with their villages that close the list of Naphtali's towns. Easton's Bible Dictionary and the International Standard Bible…

Hosah was a town on the boundary of the tribe of Asher, named in the description of Asher's territory in Josh 19:29. The border is traced past Ramah and the fortified city of Tyre, then turns to Hosah before running out to the sea near Achzib. This places Hosah near Tyre on the Phoenician coast.…

Hukkok was a town on the boundary of the tribe of Naphtali in Galilee. It appears only once, in Josh 19:34, where Naphtali's border runs west from Aznoth-tabor to Hukkok and then meets Zebulun on the south and Asher on the west. Smith's Bible Dictionary and the International Standard Bible…

Hukok was a city named in 1 Chr 6:75 alongside Rehob, each given "with her suburbs" (its surrounding pasturelands). From the surrounding list, it was one of the towns in the territory of Asher assigned to the Levite family of Gershon. The parallel list of Levitical cities in Josh 21:31 names…

Humtah was a town in the hill country of Judah, named only once in the Bible, in the list of cities allotted to the tribe of Judah (Josh 15:54). It appears in a group of nine towns with their villages that includes Hebron (also called Kirjath-arba) and Zior. Smith's Bible Dictionary gives the…

Idalah was a city in the territory of the tribe of Zebulun. It appears only once, in the list of Zebulun's towns in Josh 19:15, where it is named between Shimron and Bethlehem (the Bethlehem of Galilee, not the Bethlehem of Judah). Nothing else is recorded about it. Its exact site is uncertain.…

Idumea is the Greek form of the name Edom, the land of the descendants of Esau. Easton's Bible Dictionary notes that the King James Version also uses "Idumea" in Isa 34:5–6 and Ezek 35:15; 36:5, where newer translations have "Edom." In the New Testament it appears once. Mark 3:8 lists it among the…

Iim was a town in the far south of Judah, named once in the list of cities given to the tribe of Judah, between Baalah and Azem (Josh 15:29). Easton's Bible Dictionary places it in the south of Judah, and the Tyndale House STEPBible names list places it in the Negev region, in line with the…

Illyricum was a Roman region on the eastern shore of the Adriatic Sea, northwest of Macedonia, covering much of present-day Croatia, Bosnia and Albania. It appears in the Bible only in Rom 15:19, where Paul says that he had fully preached the gospel of Christ from Jerusalem "round about unto…

Iphtah, spelled Jiphtah in the King James Version, was a town in the lowland hill country (the Shephelah) of Judah. It appears only once, in the list of towns given to the tribe of Judah, where it is named alongside Ashnah and Nezib (Josh 15:43). The International Standard Bible Encyclopedia (1915)…

Ir-shemesh, meaning "city of the sun" according to Smith's Bible Dictionary, was a town in the territory given to the tribe of Dan. It is named in Josh 19:41, alongside Zorah and Eshtaol, at the start of the list of Dan's towns. Smith's Bible Dictionary and the International Standard Bible…

Irpeel was a town in the territory of the tribe of Benjamin. It appears only once, in the list of Benjamin's cities in Josh 18:27, between Rekem and Taralah. By inference from that list, it belonged to the group of Benjamite towns in the hill country north and west of Jerusalem. The name is usually…

Ithlah (spelled Jethlah in the King James Version) was a town assigned to the tribe of Dan. It appears only once, in the list of Danite towns in Josh 19:42, next to Shaalabbin and Aijalon (Ajalon). That places it in the western foothills toward the coastal plain. Easton's Bible Dictionary gives the…
